question: Can one image-global Gaussian optimal-transport map in the exact zero-luminance chroma plane retain AO6 style while avoiding the closed one-angle and pixelwise-direction failure modes?

operator.basis: deterministic orthonormal basis of the Rec.709 zero-luminance plane
operator.statistics: full-image float64 population mean and covariance of CB11 and AO6 chroma coordinates
operator.transport: closed-form symmetric positive-definite Gaussian 2-Wasserstein map from CB11 chroma distribution to AO6 chroma distribution
operator.scale: one maximum analytical per-pixel safe step from CB11 to the global Gaussian target
operator.forbidden: local statistics, pixel correspondence fit, covariance ridge, eigenvalue clipping, iterative flow, semantic mask, learned model, magnitude cap or post-score rescue

research_basis.colorfm: arXiv:2607.07119, flow-matching colour transfer as a current explicit-transport research comparator
research_basis.modflows: AAAI 2025 / arXiv:2503.19062, invertible optimal-transport colour mapping as a current explicit-transport comparator
research_basis.position: clean-room analytic Gaussian transport baseline; no paper code, model, weights or novelty claim

stop_rules: Any covariance or transport-envelope failure closes the exact analytic operator before render evaluation.
Any automatic failure closes before visual preference.
Any severe or preference failure closes without ridge, eigenvalue clipping, local statistics or post-score rescue.
Pass opens only a wholly new source confirmation.
claim_ceiling: Development-only image-global Gaussian chroma-transport evidence on consumed CC0 display proxies; not fresh confirmation, stock response, calibration, population preference or product promotion.
